parsing_res_list.block_content: Table 5.8 End-point Constraints for a Cubic Spline

Description of the strategyEquations involving $ m_{0} $ and $ m_{N} $
(i) Clamped cubic spline: specify $ S^{\prime }(x_{0}) $, $ S^{\prime }(x_{n}) $(the “best choice" if the derivatives are known)$ m_{0}=\frac {3}{h_{0}}(d_{0}\quad S^{\prime }(x_{0}))\frac {m_{1}}{2} m_{N}=\frac{3}{h_{N\quad1}}(S^{\prime}(x_{N})\quad d_{N\quad1})\quad\frac{m_{N\quad1}}{2} $
(ii) Natural cubic spline(a"relaxed curve")$ m_{0}=0,m_{N}=0 $
(iii) Extrapolate $ S^{\prime \prime }(x) $to theendpoints$ m_{0}=m_{1}\quad\frac {h_{0}(m_{2}\quad m_{1})}{h_{1}}, m_{N}=m_{N\quad1}+\frac{h_{N\quad1}(m_{N\quad1}\quad m_{N\quad2})}{h_{N\quad2}} $
(iv) $ S^{\prime \prime }(x) $ is constant near theendpoints$ m_{0}=m_{1},m_{N}=m_{N\quad1} $
(v) Specify $ S^{\prime \prime }(X) $ at eachendpoint$ m_{0}=S^{\prime \prime }(x_{0}),m_{N}=S^{\prime \prime }(x_{N}) $
Equations (13) and (14) with (12) used for  $ k = 2, 3, \ldots, N $ 2 form N 1 linear equations involving the coefficients  $ m_{1}, m_{2}, \ldots, m_{N-1} $.

Regardless of the particular strategy chosen in Table 5.8, we can rewrite equations 1 and N-1 in (12) and obtain a tridiagonal linear system of the form  $ HM = V $, which involves  $ m_1, m_2, \ldots, m_N $.
